ENGLISH LANGUAGE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #15
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. run
   B. blue
   C. happiness
   D. quickly

2. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goed
   B. went
   C. goes
   D. going

3. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a joining word
   B. Only an action
   C. A person, place, thing, or idea
   D. Only a describing word

4. When practising Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

5. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.

6. When practising Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.

7. When practising Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing.

8. When practising Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

9. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. One main idea with supporting sentences
   B. Many unrelated topics with no link
   C. Only one word repeated
   D. No full stops

10. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

11. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. where is the library
   B. Where is the library?
   C. Where is the Library
   D. Where is the library

12. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 7.3.1 Word classes: verb aspect and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of writing: Punctuation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 8.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary: and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. A — run

2. B — went

3. C — A person, place, thing, or idea

4. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

5. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.

6. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.

7. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing.

8. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

9. A — One main idea with supporting sentences

10. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

11. B — Where is the library?

12. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Grammar in Use 7.3.1 Word classes: verb aspect; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of writing: Punctuation; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening and Speaking 8.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary:; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
